setup: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Cross one leg in front of the other, planting both feet flat on the floor side by side with toes pointing forward.
Keep the rear leg straight while allowing a soft, slight bend in the front knee.
steps: Hinge at your hips and slowly lower your torso toward your knees.
Reach your hands toward the floor, your shins, or a yoga block until you feel a gentle to moderate stretch along the posterior thigh and outer hip of the back leg.
Hold the position statically, maintaining balanced weight distribution across both feet.
Slowly engage your glutes and roll or hinge back up to the starting position, then switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, using each exhalation to relax deeper into the stretch without forcing range.
cues: Hinge from the hips before rounding

common_faults.fault: Bending the rear knee, which reduces tension on the targeted hamstring.
common_faults.correction: Keep the back leg fully straight while keeping its heel firmly pressed into the floor.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing or using momentum to force the reach deeper.
common_faults.correction: Ease into a comfortable stretch threshold and maintain a steady, static hold.

precautions: Perform near a wall or sturdy surface if balance is unstable while folding forward.

name: Standing Cross-Legged Hamstring Stretch
summary: A standing flexibility exercise that stretches the hamstrings, glutes, and lateral hip of the rear leg by folding forward with crossed legs.
